question.problem:
Find the value of the double sum

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij})
$$

given that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8}  a_{ij} = 8, \qquad\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8}  b_{ij} = 15.
$$
question.worked_solution:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}(1+2{a}_{ij}-{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}1+{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}2{a}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}{b}_{ij} \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}1)+2{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}{a}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}{b}_{ij} \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}1)+2(8)-15 \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}1)+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 1 = mn,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sum }_{j=1}^{8}1)+1 & =5\cdot 8+1 \\  & =40+1 \\  & =41.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij}) = 41.
$$
